trigger: Suspected compromise of any device, account, or media used for Client A work, or any contact seeking Client A security or system information
notify: Client A cyber security contact, then the contractor coordinator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the main clock in this runbook. It lets Client A meet its own 10 CFR 73.77 clocks

trigger: Suspected unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client B security information, including through a compromised laptop or suite account
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Client B security information was on the laptop or in the suite at the time (working notes, any copies)

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification (Client A's duty)
trigger: Cyber attack that adversely impacted or could have impacted safety, security, or emergency preparedness functions; insider-initiated attack; notice to another agency; intelligence gathering or pre-operational planning
deadline: 1 hour; 4 hours; 8 hours; corrective action program entry within 24 hours
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS (by Client A)
applies_at_this_tier: No - covers licensees subject to 73.54 or 73.110. Client A decides; the owner gives Client A the facts fast (row 1). Proposed rule 91 FR 38928 would replace these specific notifications (not final)

trigger: Actual or attempted theft, sabotage, or diversion; or suspicious activity related to possible theft, sabotage, or diversion of a category 1 or 2 quantity
deadline: LLEA immediately (actual or attempted) or as appropriate (suspicious); regulator no later than 4 hours
notify: Local law enforcement, then the regulator (by Client B; under Florida's license condition event reports go to the Bureau of Radiation Control)
applies_at_this_tier: No - Client B's duty. If an attacker may have seen Client B's security plan, Client B assesses it as possible suspicious activity; the owner's 24-hour report (row 2) starts that

trigger: Questionable behavior or activity of another person with Client A access, such as the per-diem technician asking for the owner's portal access or media
deadline: Report to Client A (no fixed clock in the rule; treat as part of the 8-hour report)
notify: Client A reviewing official or the owner's Client A supervisor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the owner holds unescorted access

trigger: Any document or file marked Safeguards Information reaches the owner
notify: Client A (or the sender) by phone; follow their return instructions
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if it happens; none held today. POL-01 8.4 steps

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of a Florida resident (the per-diem technician's name and Social Security number on the W-9)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the W-9 copy was in the compromised email or accounting account

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds one individual's personal information

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: The accounting SaaS vendor has a breach of a system it maintains for the business
deadline: No later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound; the owner then gives the row 7 notice

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Any thought of paying an extortion demand
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

trigger: Credential theft or account takeover affecting a nuclear plant contractor
deadline: As soon as practical, after Client A is told
notify: FBI (IC3 online report or local field office)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; coordinate with Client A first because the plant may already be reporting

obligation: CIRCIA covered incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed the business is below the SBA standard and owns no reactor or fuel cycle facility

trigger: Covered equipment found while performing a federal contract
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
